## What the caller sees

This is the default `detail` sent in the problem+json response, verbatim:

The replay did not reproduce the recorded run. The difference report names every value that differs.

## What to do as a developer

Guidance for the engineer who hit this code. It is non-normative: it is never
sent on the wire and does not constrain an implementation. Wire behaviour is
defined only by `spec/heph-spec.md` and the conformance vectors.

A replay compared its result against a provenance record and they differ. Read the difference report before anything else, because it names each differing value and that naming is the finding. Do not re-run hoping for a match, and do not call the run flaky until the report says a result value differs rather than an input hash. A differing config\_hash, data\_hash, deps\_hash or code\_sha means you replayed against different inputs, different dependencies or different code, so reconcile those first. The environment is descriptive and is never compared, so a different platform, runtime version or accelerator is not what caused this. A provenance-only run never promised a match, so check the record's class before treating a divergence as a defect.
